question: Your customer support resolution agent handles a billing dispute that spans six orders. Before it decides on process_refund, it builds one long input that joins the get_customer result and six lookup_order results. The decision uses details from the first and last orders correctly, but it ignores a duplicate charge recorded in the fourth order, even though the input fits well within the context window. Which two changes to the aggregated input best address this problem?

options.text: Switch to a model with a larger context window so that each of the six order results receives more attention.
options.reason: The input already fits in the context window. The missed finding comes from the lost in the middle effect, so the cause is its position in the input and a larger window leaves that position effect in place.

options.text: Place a summary of the key findings from all six order lookups at the beginning of the aggregated input.
options.reason: Models reliably process the beginning of long inputs, so a key findings summary placed first keeps middle findings visible and mitigates position effects.

options.text: Condense all six order results into one brief progressive summary so that the input becomes short enough to process reliably.
options.reason: Progressive summarization risks turning amounts, dates and statuses into vague statements, so the agent could lose the duplicate charge.

options.text: Remove the earlier conversation history from the request so that the order results make up a larger share of the input.
options.reason: The guide says that complete conversation history must be passed in later requests to keep the conversation coherent. Removing it leaves the middle findings in the middle.

options.text: Organize the detailed order results under explicit section headers so that the data for each order is clearly labeled.
options.reason: The guide recommends explicit section headers for detailed results. They mitigate the lost in the middle effect, and this complements the summary placed at the beginning.
